beats.name: Arthur Samuel
beats.role: IBM engineer who coined the term 'machine learning'

beats.text: He coined it to describe a draughts program, written for the IBM 701, that got better by remembering which positions led to wins.
beats.note: Memory was so tight he had to invent an early form of what is now called alpha-beta pruning.

beats.context: how far IBM's share price rose overnight after the program was first demonstrated.

beats.text: It improved by playing thousands of games against itself.
beats.note: Samuel kept refining it until the mid-1970s.

beats.text: In 1962 it beat Robert Nealey. IBM's own history calls him only a 'self-described' checkers master.
beats.note: Its record against humans after that was mixed: a respectable amateur, not a world beater.

beats.line: Machine learning was named after a draughts program.
